mg_hub_faq.q: Why Magento 2 and not Shopify or WooCommerce?
mg_hub_faq.a: Magento gives you data ownership and full control over the catalog, pricing, and custom logic — without monthly platform fees like Shopify Plus. Once a shop crosses 5–10k SKUs, multistore, and complex B2B/B2C scenarios, Magento pays off. For smaller shops run by a marketing team, Shopify or WooCommerce is often the better choice.

mg_hub_faq.q: Hyvä or Luma — what do you recommend?
mg_hub_faq.a: Hyvä by default for new shops and most redesigns. Hyvä is 3–5× faster than Luma, builds quicker, and development hurts less. We optimize Luma only when there's a real reason (e.g. lots of existing custom modules without a Hyvä compat layer).

mg_hub_faq.q: How long does an M1 → M2 migration take?
mg_hub_faq.a: Realistic range: 8–20 weeks, depending on the number of extensions, custom logic, and data migration scope. Before we quote we do an audit (1–2 weeks) and only then commit to a timeline.

mg_hub_faq.q: How much does development or migration cost?
mg_hub_faq.a: After the audit we offer fixed price or T&M with a ceiling. For migrations we usually go fixed price, since scope is known; for new development T&M with sprint pricing tends to work better.

mg_hub_faq.q: What kind of post-launch support do you offer?
mg_hub_faq.a: Three SLA tiers: Bronze (best-effort, quarterly health check), Silver (monthly health check + security patches in 72h), Gold (24/7 on-call + monthly release window). Details after the first call.

mg_hub_faq.q: Do you handle GDPR and PCI compliance?
mg_hub_faq.a: Yes. GDPR: data retention policies, anonymization scripts, cookie consent integrations. PCI: we never store card numbers — we use Stripe/Adyen/AllSecure tokenization, plus we configure TLS, headers, and logging per PCI DSS 4.0.

mg_int_patterns_subtitle: These aren't buzzwords — they're what stops an integration from breaking on Black Friday peak.

mg_int_patterns.title: Queue + retry pattern
mg_int_patterns.desc: ERP sync always goes through a queue (RabbitMQ or Magento queue). Retry with exponential backoff and a dead-letter queue for messages that can't be processed.

mg_int_patterns.title: Idempotent endpoint design
mg_int_patterns.desc: Every state-changing POST has an `Idempotency-Key` or equivalent. If a carrier sends a webhook 3 times — the order stays in the same state.

mg_int_patterns.title: OAuth2 / JWT auth layers
mg_int_patterns.desc: No shared API keys in messaging apps — every integration partner has its own credential set and rotation path.

mg_int_patterns.title: Structured logs + correlation ID
mg_int_patterns.desc: Every message in the integration carries a `correlation_id` visible in Magento, the ERP, and Sentry. Debugging becomes minutes, not days.

mg_int_patterns.title: Queue depth + error rate alerts
mg_int_patterns.desc: Sentry + custom Magento dashboards track queue depth, retry count, and error rate. Alerts fire before customers report a problem.

mg_int_patterns.title: OpenAPI / JSON Schema contracts
mg_int_patterns.desc: Every API leaving Magento has an OpenAPI definition in the `docs/` repo — used to generate clients and validators.

mg_int_pitfalls_subtitle: Things we've seen on real projects — now we track them up front.

mg_int_pitfalls.title: Sync in the request thread
mg_int_pitfalls.desc: Direct ERP sync from a `place_order` observer — if ERP goes down, customers can't checkout. It must go through a queue.

mg_int_pitfalls.title: Plain-text API keys in code
mg_int_pitfalls.desc: Magento `env.php` / GitHub history full of tokens. We replace this with Vault or Magento Encryption Key + DB config.

mg_int_pitfalls.title: No API versioning
mg_int_pitfalls.desc: Partner changes the shape, everything breaks. Versioning (`/v1`, `/v2`) and a deprecation window are mandatory.

mg_int_pitfalls.title: "Silent" log errors
mg_int_pitfalls.desc: A catch-all `try/catch` that logs a warning and continues as if nothing happened — the order is silently lost. Errors must be visible.

mg_int_pitfalls.title: Missing rate limiting
mg_int_pitfalls.desc: Webhook bombing from a partner system takes Magento down. Rate limiting + circuit breakers are the default.

mg_int_faq.q: Do you do integrations without rewriting existing modules?
mg_int_faq.a: Whenever possible — yes. We use the Magento plugin system, observers, and custom API layers. Existing modules are touched only when their implementation directly blocks us (e.g. tight coupling in the payment flow).

mg_int_faq.q: How long does a typical integration take?
mg_int_faq.a: ERP integration with standard entities: 4–8 weeks. Payments / carriers: 1–3 weeks per provider. Custom API layer: depends on the number of endpoints, but we ship iteratively (endpoint by endpoint, never "big bang").

mg_int_faq.q: What if the partner has a poor API?
mg_int_faq.a: We build an adapter layer between the partner API and Magento — with retry, shape normalization, and a mock server for QA. If the partner only has CSV / SFTP, we build a file-based integration with the same queue + retry approach.
You — everything we ship lands in your GitHub/GitLab repo, with a MIT-style internal-use license. No vendor lock-in.

mg_perf_bottlenecks.title: FPC bypass on a whole category
mg_perf_bottlenecks.desc: A custom module sets a `noCache` flag on a PLP — and suddenly every request hits Magento. Audit + targeted invalidation fixes it.

mg_perf_bottlenecks.title: Reindex blocking write operations
mg_perf_bottlenecks.desc: Indexer in "Update on Save" mode runs synchronously inside the order placement flow. Switch to "Update by Schedule" + cron tuning.

mg_perf_bottlenecks.desc: A full reindex runs during the day, search drops. Schedule + partial reindex for routine updates.

mg_perf_faq.q: How much improvement is realistic on an existing shop?
mg_perf_faq.a: Typically 40–70% TTFB improvement and 30–50% LCP improvement in the first 2–4 weeks. Real numbers come after the audit, not before. If a shop has never been tuned, 2× faster first paint is common.

mg_perf_faq.q: Do I have to move to Hyvä to get good performance?
mg_perf_faq.a: No — Luma can be fast if it's tuned properly. But if a redesign is on the roadmap in the next two years, Hyvä is the default: 60–80% smaller JS bundle, easier maintenance, better Core Web Vitals out of the box.

mg_perf_faq.q: What if I'm on shared hosting?
mg_perf_faq.a: Magento on shared hosting is hard to tune properly (no control over PHP-FPM, Redis, Varnish). We usually recommend moving to a VPS first, then tuning. The exception is Magento-specific shared hosting (e.g. Nexcess).

mg_perf_faq.q: Do you do that "instant page load" thing other shops have?
mg_perf_faq.a: Yes — a combination of Hyvä + ESI + Varnish + preload of critical assets + speculation rules for PLP→PDP navigation. Not magic, just serious caching.

mg_perf_faq.q: How much does a performance engagement cost?
mg_perf_faq.a: Audit: fixed price (~3–5 days of work). Implementation: T&M or sprint pricing — usually 2–4 weeks for the first pass. After that we recommend a monthly retainer (8–16 hours/month) for upkeep.

mg_b2b_faq_subtitle: What clients ask most often before a B2B implementation.

mg_b2b_faq.q: Do I need an Adobe Commerce license for B2B features?
mg_b2b_faq.a: Yes — the B2B layer (company accounts, quote workflow, shared catalogs, requisition lists) is part of Adobe Commerce, not Magento Open Source. Licensing starts around $22k/yr (revenue-based). Some extensions emulate part of B2B on Open Source, but for serious B2B we recommend the Commerce license.

mg_b2b_faq.q: How long does a B2B implementation take?
mg_b2b_faq.a: Realistic range: 12–24 weeks for a standard B2B implementation, 6+ months if it includes EDI, PunchOut, and complex ERP integrations. Before we quote, we audit the sales process — and only then commit to a timeline.

mg_b2b_faq.q: Can B2B and B2C run on the same shop?
mg_b2b_faq.a: Yes — the most common setup is a "mixed" shop: B2C customers register the classic way, B2B customers via company-account registration. Magento can segment by customer group what each one sees (prices, catalog, payment methods).

mg_b2b_faq.q: How does the price from the ERP sync to the shop in real-time?
mg_b2b_faq.a: Three approaches: 1) cache + scheduled sync every 5–15 min, 2) ERP push on every update via webhook, 3) on-demand call to the ERP API at add-to-cart. We pick based on the number of SKUs, request volume, and the guarantees the ERP offers.

mg_b2b_faq.q: Do you support Hyvä on B2B?
mg_b2b_faq.a: Yes. Hyvä B2B supports all standard Adobe Commerce B2B features (company accounts, quotes, shared catalogs). Hyvä Checkout is especially valuable here because it seriously speeds up a B2B checkout with many line items.

mg_b2b_faq.q: What happens to the existing B2B email/Excel process?
mg_b2b_faq.a: We don't kill it overnight — that triggers sales-team pushback. We go gradually: first top 20 clients on the shop, then expand. The sales team uses the shop as a tool (they can create a quote on behalf of the customer), not as a replacement.
